results.name: ior1_is_invisible
results.claim: With IOR 1, saturation 1 and no dispersion, frost, tint or light terms, the glass shows exactly the refraction TOP.

results.name: ior1_is_invisible_with_wobble
results.claim: Ripples do not undo the silhouette fix: at IOR 1 the rippled glass is still invisible (normals are turned toward the camera after the wobble).

results.name: opacity0_is_invisible
results.claim: Opacity 0 removes the glass entirely, reflections included.

results.name: no_refraction_top_blends_clear
results.claim: With no refraction TOP, clear untinted glass with no light terms blends to the real background (alpha 0).

results.name: samples_invariant_without_dispersion
results.claim: Without dispersion or frost, every sample is identical, so the sample count cannot change the image.

results.name: morph1_equals_target
results.claim: Morph 1 toward a preset renders that preset.

results.name: morph0_is_neutral
results.claim: Morph 0 leaves the current look unchanged.

results.name: morph_frame_is_smooth_after_an_hour
results.claim: One frame of a 100-frame A/B morph (Morph 0.50 to 0.51 in 1/60 s) changes the image no more after an hour than after 2 s: the ripple and film drift is integrated, so changing its speed never throws the pattern. (rate x speed x absolute time jumped up to 226/255 in the final image and 255/255 in the film.)

results.name: speed_change_is_smooth_after_an_hour
results.claim: After an hour, nudging Wobble speed from 0.60 to 0.61 changes one frame no more than one frame of motion at a fixed speed does (Aqua Jelly, normal stage). (Previously up to 79/255.)

results.name: backface_thickness_matches_chord
results.claim: With the back-face pass, thickness equals the exact chord length through a unit sphere (within 3/255).

results.name: backface_thickness_matches_chord_far
results.claim: At 50 units from the camera the measured thickness still equals the exact chord (within 2/255): distances are stored as 32-bit floats.

results.name: backface_thickness_matches_chord_orthographic
results.claim: With an orthographic camera, measured thickness equals the chord along the parallel rays, off axis too (within 3/255).

results.name: backface_pass_adds_no_dark_fringe
results.claim: Over a uniform grey scene, clear glass with the back-face pass stays exactly grey: the back-face lookup never blends in the empty background (knot, IOR 1.5).

results.name: wobble_independent_of_object_scale
results.claim: Wobble tilts the normals by the same amount whether the object is scaled 0.1, 1 or 10 by its Geometry COMP, the camera moved with it and Object size set to the scale, as Fit to Glass geometry sets it (normal stage).

results.name: faceted_fallback_without_normals
results.claim: Geometry without normals gets faceted normals from screen derivatives, close to the smooth normals and the same at any scale (sphere, 0.1 vs 1).

results.name: frost_converges_with_samples
results.claim: Frost 0.6 is a continuous blur: 12 and 32 samples agree within 16/255 at every pixel. (Without the mipmap widening, ghost copies make them differ by up to 31/255.)

results.name: dispersion_converges_with_samples
results.claim: Dispersion 1 at the default 12 samples agrees with a 64-sample render: no glass pixel differs by more than 32/255, and the mean difference stays within 1/255 (2.5/255 with Thickness 2.5), on Clear Crystal and Prism Chrome (refraction stage, torus). A blurring mip level on the rainbow fan (tried in the family sync, from the blobs study) failed this: up to 377 pixels over 32/255 and twice the mean error.

results.name: energy_conserving_mirror_is_pure_reflection
results.claim: With Energy conserving on and Mirror 1, nothing shows through: the final image equals the reflection stage.

results.name: srgb_colour_mode_decodes_colours
results.claim: Colour parameters set to sRGB render like the same colours converted to linear by hand (Violet Gel, body stage).

results.name: transparent_scene_stays_transparent
results.claim: Over a Refraction TOP with a transparent background (alpha 0), invisible glass (IOR 1, no tint or light terms) leaves the image exactly as the scene: colour and alpha, with the back-face pass off and on. (The 6a58487 material wrote alpha 1, so clear glass turned the empty background opaque black. Until fix V1 the back-face pass did the same: max 255/255 on 93,845 pixels.) Measured, not asserted: where the scene is only partly covered (alpha 0.5, as on antialiased edges), the glass draws the bent scene and blending adds the scene behind it again by the glass's see-through share, so the pixel comes out brighter and more opaque (a documented limit).

results.name: empty_scene_matches_no_refraction_top
results.claim: Where the Refraction TOP is empty (alpha 0), the glass blends exactly as it does with no Refraction TOP connected (Violet Gel, colour and alpha): one formula covers both. Measured, not asserted: with the back-face pass on, alpha still matches, but the inner surface's own reflections show over the empty scene; with no Refraction TOP the material reads nothing behind it, inner surface included.

results.name: opaque_scene_matches_pre_sync
results.claim: Over an opaque Refraction TOP (alpha 1, the demo backdrop), each of the twelve presets renders as the 6a58487 material did, within 1/255 (knot), with the back-face pass off and on.

results.name: extra_colour_buffers_get_zeros
results.claim: In a render with three colour buffers (TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS 3, cleared to 0.5, blending off), buffer 0 holds exactly the single-buffer glass and buffers 1 and 2 hold zeros wherever the glass is drawn (with the material's premultiplied blending, zeros leave those buffers unchanged). The 6a58487 material wrote buffer 0 only.

results.name: output_fits_half_float
results.claim: A light colour of 200,000 (a typed value, or an HDR multiplier) still gives finite colour no higher than 1024 in an rgba16float render (half floats end at 65504; the 6a58487 material wrote infinity there). The cap is on colour only: the back-face pass of a sphere 1500 units away still stores distances above 1400 in alpha.

results.name: bends_follow_screen_orientation
results.claim: A build whose screen y runs opposite to the projection (emulated: the rasteriser flips y, and the scene render and back-face pass come from the same build) renders the exact mirror image: bends, frost, the flat-image reflection and the back-face pass all follow (at most 1000 pixels over 8/255; the multisample pattern is not mirrored, so bright antialiased rims differ on about 650 pixels even where the image is right). The 6a58487 material bent light the wrong way up there (about 73,000 pixels).

results.name: flip_v_corrects_upside_down_inputs
results.claim: If the Refraction TOP and the back-face pass arrive upside down relative to the render (normal raster, or a flipped raster with upright inputs), Flip V restores the normal image: it flips the base screen UV and every vertical offset together. (The 6a58487 Flip V flipped the UV only, which is right only for the second case.)

results.name: screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels
results.claim: The measured screen orientation is right at every glass pixel but a known few, on the centre lines too: the twelve presets (each at its own pose) on the torus, the knot and the sphere, in a normal and a flipped raster, at 480 x 270 and at the odd size 481 x 271. One sample per pixel (the glass alone): at most 2 wrong pixels per row of twelve renders. Four samples (the canvas, like an antialiased Render TOP): at most 10 per row (20 until the family critic's centre-line round; measured: at most 8). The few left are a centre-line pixel on a nearly edge-on surface (the tie keeps +1) and silhouette pixels where the glass covers one to three samples of four: the pixel is shaded at its centre, outside its triangle, so its point can project to the other side of a centre line (the Liquid Glass Flow finding). Whether they are visible in TouchDesigner is a family open question with a pending native check (co-design.json; validation.json, centre_line_residual). The family sync's comparison with +1 on ties was wrong on the whole centre row of the odd size in a flipped raster (about 1,500 pixels per row). Same test and thresholds as Liquid Glass Lit. The 6a58487 material assumed the usual orientation and is wrong at every pixel of a flipped raster.

results.name: fog_adds_only_the_glass_share
results.claim: With full fog (preview stand-in) on invisible glass at Opacity 0.5, every glass pixel is half the scene plus half the fog colour within 2/255 (only antialiased silhouette pixels, which mix glass and scene, are neither), and at Opacity 0 the fogged glass leaves no trace. With fog off, TDFog changes nothing (opaque_scene_matches_pre_sync). The 6a58487 material ignored fog. TouchDesigner's own fog is a native check.

results.name: object_size_carries_presets_over
results.claim: A preset looks the same on an object built 0.1 or 10 units across, with Object size set to match (what Fit to Glass geometry measures): bend, frost, tint, ripples and film all follow (final image, at most 50 pixels over 8/255). The 6a58487 material had no Object size: its bend and tint stayed in scene units.

results.name: fit_size_carries_presets_over_comp_scale
results.claim: A preset looks the same on an object scaled 0.1 or 10 by its Geometry COMP, with Object size set to that scale (what Fit to Glass geometry sets) and the camera moved with it: the ripples (normal stage), the film bands (film stage) and the final image, within 2/255 at every pixel (measured: 1/255), and so at most 50 pixels over 8/255 (the family's shared clause). The pattern frequencies are multiplied by the world scale, so Object size means the same world size for the patterns as for Thickness, Frost and Tint density (the family rule, Liquid Glass Lit decisions.json family_rule). Ported from Liquid Glass Lit.

results.name: comp_scale_at_object_size_1_gives_k_times_the_patterns
results.claim: An object scaled k times by its Geometry COMP but left at Object size 1 shows k times as many ripples and film bands as on the unscaled demo: finer for k = 10 (pattern detail at least 4 times the unscaled count), coarser for k = 0.1 (at most 0.4 times). With Object size 10, what Fit sets, COMP scale 10 gives the unscaled count within 2%. Aqua Jelly normal stage and Oil Slick film stage, camera moved with the scale. This pins the direction the README troubleshooting note and the G1 record state; the c94e849 shaders give ratio 1 at Object size 1.

results.name: backdrop_menu_switches_the_demo_scene
results.claim: Study > Backdrop: Checker (the default) is the 6a58487 backdrop exactly; Type is a black page with heavy white type (most pixels dark, at least 5% white ink), the backdrop of the Liquid Glass Prism study, so the family's contact sheets compare. The 6a58487 backdrop had no menu.

results.name: render_pass_keeps_foreground_in_front
results.claim: An opaque ball between the camera and the glass (demo torus, Prism Chrome): with the README's Render Pass TOP route (the glass drawn into the scene render, whose depth is kept), the image shows the ball exactly as the scene render does wherever it covers the glass (within 2/255). Control: laid over the scene with an Over TOP (the fallback, and the demo's own route), the glass is drawn over the ball (more than 40/255). Same emulation, ball and thresholds as Liquid Glass Prism and Flow. TouchDesigner's own Render Pass TOP is a native check.

results.name: film_swirl_frequency_0_is_one_drifting_thickness
results.claim: uFilm.w = 0 (film swirl frequency, set by hand) gives one film thickness over the whole object, no swirl: on a flat sheet seen at one angle the film stage is one colour (within 2/255), where the default 2.5 swirls it. That one thickness still drifts with uPhase.w: from 2 s to 30 s every sheet pixel changes colour (Prism Chrome, Wobble speed 0.3). Wobble speed 0 stops the drift. So 0 does not freeze the film; Wobble speed 0 does. Ported from Liquid Glass Flow.

results.name: screen_uv_matches_pixel
results.claim: screenUV() gives the pixel position over the render size (preview viewport stand-in).

scope: Shader maths and study.json bindings in WebGL2 (SwiftShader). Not a TouchDesigner render.
